# Security [»](https://docs.spacelift.io/product/security\#security "Anchor link to this section")

At Spacelift, your security while using our service is our first and foremost priority. Here's what we're doing to maintain your trust by keeping Spacelift [secure by design](https://spacelift.io/security).

You can access security reports, compliance information, and controls details in our [Trust Center](https://trust.spacelift.io/).

## Certifications [»](https://docs.spacelift.io/product/security\#certifications "Anchor link to this section")

Spacelift is **SOC2 Type II Certified**.

Certification performed by an independent external auditor, who confirms the effectiveness of internal controls in terms of **Spacelift Security: Confidentiality, Integrity, Availability, and Privacy of customer data.**

## Security audits [»](https://docs.spacelift.io/product/security\#security-audits "Anchor link to this section")

Spacelift performs regular security audits using:

- Automated security tooling.
- Internal audits by the Spacelift security team.
- External security firms for audits and penetration testing at least once per year.

### CVEs [»](https://docs.spacelift.io/product/security\#cves "Anchor link to this section")

It is expected that critical and high-severity CVEs will periodically affect operating system images and infrastructure components. Spacelift continuously monitors for newly disclosed vulnerabilities and regularly rebuilds and publishes updated images containing the necessary security patches and mitigations.

Customers are responsible for ensuring they use the most up-to-date image versions provided by Spacelift, as updated images are released on a regular basis, usually weekly.

Spacelift targets remediation SLAs of:

- **7 days** for vulnerabilities classified as **Critical**
- **30 days** for vulnerabilities classified as **High**

We are using CVSS 3.0 for classification. Vulnerability severity and prioritization may vary depending on internal risk assessment, exploitability, vendor guidance, environmental exposure, and operational impact. In some cases, remediation timelines may also depend on upstream vendor fixes or third-party dependency availability.

## Encryption [»](https://docs.spacelift.io/product/security\#encryption "Anchor link to this section")

All of Spacelift's data is encrypted in transit and at rest. All traffic is handled using secure transport protocols with the exception of intra-VPC traffic between the web server and the load balancer, which is protected by a restrictive [AWS security group](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/userguide/VPC_SecurityGroups.html).

All the data sources (Amazon S3, database, Amazon SNS topics, and Amazon SQS queues) are encrypted at rest using [AWS KMS](https://aws.amazon.com/kms/) keys with restricted and audited access.

[Customer secrets](https://docs.spacelift.io/concepts/configuration/environment#variable-visibility) are extra encrypted at rest to keep them safe from all attackers, internal or external.

## Security features [»](https://docs.spacelift.io/product/security\#security-features "Anchor link to this section")

### Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA) [»](https://docs.spacelift.io/product/security\#multi-factor-authentication-mfa "Anchor link to this section")

This feature elevates the security of your Identity Provider (IdP) sessions by integrating the use of FIDO2 security keys, managed within Spacelift. MFA provides an additional layer of security for your identity. Designed for seamless integration, MFA can be enforced across all user accounts to maintain consistent security protocols. You can learn more about our MFA feature [here](https://docs.spacelift.io/product/security/mfa).

### Single Sign-On (SSO) [»](https://docs.spacelift.io/product/security\#single-sign-on-sso "Anchor link to this section")

In addition to the default login providers (GitHub, GitLab, Microsoft, and Google), Spacelift supports Single Sign-On (SSO) via SAML or OIDC using your favorite identity provider. Using SSO, Spacelift can be configured in a password-less approach, helping your company follow a zero-trust approach. As long as your Identity Provider supports SAML or OIDC, and passing the `email` scope, you're good to go! You can learn more about our Single Sign-On support [here](https://docs.spacelift.io/integrations/single-sign-on).

### OAuth redirect allowlist [»](https://docs.spacelift.io/product/security\#oauth-redirect-allowlist "Anchor link to this section")

The OAuth2 flow behind the [Spacelift MCP server](https://docs.spacelift.io/concepts/intelligence/spacelift-mcp/connecting) only redirects to loopback addresses and a built-in list of known client hosts, so a client can't have an authorization code sent to a host we don't recognize. If you front Spacelift with your own MCP proxy, account admins can extend that list with hostnames they control, rather than opening the flow up to arbitrary redirect targets. See [custom redirect hosts](https://docs.spacelift.io/concepts/intelligence/spacelift-mcp/connecting#custom-redirect-hosts).

### Environment variables [»](https://docs.spacelift.io/product/security\#environment-variables "Anchor link to this section")

Spacelift allows for granular control of environment variables on your [stacks](https://docs.spacelift.io/concepts/stack) either by setting [environment](https://docs.spacelift.io/concepts/configuration/environment) variables on a per-stack basis, or creating collections of variables as a [context](https://docs.spacelift.io/concepts/configuration/context). These environment variables can be either **plain** or **secret**.

### Private worker pools [»](https://docs.spacelift.io/product/security\#private-worker-pools "Anchor link to this section")

Spacelift supports the ability to host the underlying compute resources that are accessing your codebase and executing your deployments, on your own infrastructure as a [private worker pool](https://docs.spacelift.io/concepts/worker-pools). This grants customers the option of full control over the security of their deployments.

Furthermore, the image used by Spacelift private workers is [open source](https://github.com/spacelift-io/spacelift-worker-image), giving customers full transparency into their private workers.

### Access private version control systems [»](https://docs.spacelift.io/product/security\#access-private-version-control-systems "Anchor link to this section")

For customers that use privately hosted version control systems (such as on-premise installations of GitHub Enterprise or [other VCS providers](https://docs.spacelift.io/integrations/source-control/github)), Spacelift provides the ability to access your private VCS securely using [VCS agent pools](https://docs.spacelift.io/concepts/vcs-agent-pools).

A single VCS agent pool is a way for Spacelift to communicate with a single VCS system on your side. You run VCS agents inside of your infrastructure and configure them with your internal VCS system endpoint. They will then connect to a gateway on our backend, and we will be able to access your VCS system through them.

Spacelift VCS agent pools utilize gRPC on HTTP2 for secure, high-performance connectivity.

### Policies [»](https://docs.spacelift.io/product/security\#policies "Anchor link to this section")

Spacelift policies provide a way to express rules as code to manage your infrastructure-as-code environment. Users can build policies to control Spacelift login permissions, access controls, deployment workflows, and even govern the infrastructure itself to be deployed. Policies are based on the [Open Policy Agent](https://www.openpolicyagent.org/) project and can be defined using its rule language _Rego_. You can learn more about policies [here](https://docs.spacelift.io/concepts/policy).

## Responsible disclosure [»](https://docs.spacelift.io/product/security\#responsible-disclosure "Anchor link to this section")

If you discover a vulnerability, we would like to know about it so we can address it as quickly as possible. We would like to ask you to help us better protect our clients and our systems.

### I found a vulnerability [»](https://docs.spacelift.io/product/security\#i-found-a-vulnerability "Anchor link to this section")

**All security reports must be submitted exclusively through our dedicated Vulnerability Disclosure Program (VDP)** on Intigriti at [https://app.intigriti.com/programs/spacelift/spaceliftvdp](https://app.intigriti.com/programs/spacelift/spaceliftvdp), where you can also find the detailed in-scope and out-of-scope classifications for your report.

When you submit a vulnerability, please:

- Provide sufficient information to reproduce the problem so we can resolve it as quickly as possible.
- **Do not** take advantage of the vulnerability or problem you have discovered, for example by downloading, deleting, or modifying other people's data.
- **Do not** reveal the problem to others until it has been resolved.
- **Do not** perform attacks on physical security, social engineering, distributed denial of service, spam, or applications of third parties.

### What we promise [»](https://docs.spacelift.io/product/security\#what-we-promise "Anchor link to this section")

- If you have followed the instructions above, we will not take any legal action against you in regard to the report.
- We will handle your report with strict confidentiality and process your personal details in line with Intigriti's platform terms.
- We will keep you informed of the progress towards resolving the problem through the Intigriti platform.
- In the public information about the reported problem, we will give your name as the discoverer of the problem (unless you desire otherwise).

While rewards are not guaranteed for reported vulnerabilities, we reserve the right to reward exceptional findings at our sole discretion.

We strive to resolve all problems as quickly as possible, and we would like you to play an active role in the ultimate publication on the problem after it is resolved.
